title: Rebuilding a nearly lost game called T-Crew
author: G3nyah
selftext:
I’m rebuilding an old online game because I want to surprise my brother, who has an intellectual disability.

When we were younger, we used to play a Korean online game called **T-Crew / Treasure Crew** together. He still remembers it, and I thought it would be amazing if I could somehow recreate that experience for him.

The problem: **the game has basically disappeared from the internet.**

So far I’ve managed to recover some old YouTube footage, screenshots, archived information and bits of documentation, but I still haven’t found a surviving original game client.

That has turned this into a weird mix of **game development, preservation and reverse engineering from old footage**.

I have some coding experience, enough to understand and review what is happening, but I’d be lying if I said I was writing most of this by hand. A large part of the project is **vibe coded / AI-assisted**.

Right now I’m using things like:

* Godot for the reconstruction
* Claude for tooling, research and evidence-analysis work
* Codex / GPT models for harder implementation and architecture problems
* local scripts/CV tooling to measure things like movement and camera behavior from the surviving videos
* deterministic tests so the AI doesn’t just keep changing things until they “look right”

I’m deliberately trying to separate what we can actually prove from the surviving footage from what the AI is guessing or what I personally remember.

It has honestly become a much bigger project than I originally expected, but also a pretty interesting experiment in how far AI-assisted development can go when you’re trying to reconstruct software with very little source material.

**The main reason I’m posting here is a long shot:**

If anyone happens to have ever played T-Crew / Treasure Crew, or has anything related to it sitting on an old PC, hard drive, backup folder, CD, etc., I would REALLY like to hear from you.

Especially:

* Old installers / game clients
* Patch or update files
* Old game folders
* Screenshots
* Gameplay recordings
* Manuals / guides
* Website files
* Anything else related to T-Crew

Even an old installer that no longer works could be extremely useful for preservation/research.

I’m not selling anything and this isn’t a commercial project. I’m basically trying to reconstruct a little piece of our childhood and eventually surprise my brother with it.

And if anyone here is interested in the AI/game-dev side of the reconstruction, I’m also happy to share how I’m approaching it.
